Even in auto mode, if FTS returns a NON-zero but tiny/garbage total for a partially-stripped query, it won't fall back to the (better) prefix path because the fallback is gated on `total == 0`.
improvements.proposed: (1) For explicit `--mode fts`, if the FTS path yields 0 rows, automatically retry the prefix path (same as auto) and tag the response `mode='fts→prefix (fts matched nothing)'` so the behavior is transparent rather than an empty screen. (2) Detect when FTS has effectively dropped the query: compare the FTS-tokenized form against the raw tokens; if FTS kept fewer than, say, half the user's tokens (because of hyphens/punctuation), proactively also run prefix and UNION/merge the candidate sets (dedupe by capture_id, FTS score first). (3) Pre-normalize the FTS query string: replace hyphens/underscores with spaces and also push the de-hyphenated joined token, so 'bit-coin' searches 'bit coin bitcoin'.
improvements.rationale: A search engine should never answer 'nothing' for a query that plainly has matches in the corpus just because the tokenizer disliked a hyphen. Graceful, transparent fallback is the difference between 'works' and 'janky'.
improvements.expected_impact: Hyphenated, punctuated, and operator-style queries return results in every mode; the response explains which strategy answered. Closes the remaining 'returns empty for no obvious reason' cases.

improvements.title: Resolve real Common Crawl crawl IDs from collinfo.json instead of synthesizing odd-ISO-week IDs
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py (crawl_ids_for_range, _iso_year_weeks); consumers src/awareness/sources/cc_index.py, src/awareness/sources/fineweb.py
improvements.current_state: crawl_ids_for_range() enumerates ISO weeks in [start,end] and emits one CC-MAIN-YYYY-WW per *odd* week (anchor_week = week if odd else week-1). Verified against the live CC catalog this is almost entirely wrong: a 30-day window ending 2026-06-08 yields ['CC-MAIN-2026-19','CC-MAIN-2026-21','CC-MAIN-2026-23'] but only 2026-21 exists; a full-2024 window yields 27 IDs (01,03,05,...) while the REAL 2024 crawls are exactly [10,18,22,26,30,33,38,42,46,51] (10 crawls at irregular weeks). The synthesized IDs do not exist, so wet.paths.gz (CommonCrawlWetAdapter._run_discovery), the CDX index (cc_index.py), and FineWeb dump= names all hit 404/empty and silently return. This single bug makes the entire historical-BODY path (CC-WET + CC-Index/WARC + FineWeb dump selection) produce ~zero data and is the core of 'has no idea how to scrape the internet'.
improvements.proposed: Replace the synthetic mapping with the authoritative crawl catalog. (1) Fetch https://index.commoncrawl.org/collinfo.json once (JSON array of {id, name, 'cdx-api', 'from','to' time bounds}). Cache it on disk under cache_dir/cc_collinfo.json with a 24h TTL; ship a bundled fallback copy so a fresh offline user still gets the known list. (2) crawl_ids_for_range(start,end) = filter catalog entries whose [from,to] coverage interval overlaps [start,end]; if collinfo lacks per-crawl date bounds, derive the crawl's anchor week from its id (CC-MAIN-YYYY-WW -> ISO week start) and keep crawls whose anchor date is within [start-21d, end] (CC crawls span ~2-4 weeks). (3) Always return only IDs present in the catalog. (4) Expose get_known_crawls() so cc_index and fineweb reuse the same validated set. (5) Add a unit test asserting crawl_ids_for_range over 2024 is a subset of the real 2024 set and never returns a non-catalog id.
improvements.rationale: Common Crawl publishes ~6-12 crawls/year at irregular ISO weeks; you cannot compute valid ids arithmetically. The catalog is the only correct source of crawl ids and also carries the precise time bounds needed for accurate range->crawl mapping.
improvements.expected_impact: Turns the historical body path from ~0 documents to working. CC-WET discovery hits real wet.paths.gz (each crawl ~90k WET shards, each shard ~30-50k text docs), CC-Index CDX queries hit valid -index endpoints, and FineWeb dump= names become valid. This is the highest-leverage fix for 'actually scrapes the internet'.

improvements.title: Treat 404/empty discovery as a health signal instead of a silent successful no-op
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py, gdelt.py, cc_index.py, warc_repair.py, feeds.py; src/awareness/workers/engine.py (_run_task); new src/awareness/sources/health.py
improvements.current_state: Every adapter responds to a non-200 / 404 / empty body with a bare `return` (e.g. cc_wet_paths_not_found, gdelt_slot_missing, cc_index_query_failed). The worker then marks the task COMPLETED with docs_emitted=0. There is no aggregate signal distinguishing 'ran fine, nothing matched' from 'every fetch 404'd because the ids are wrong'. A user sees jobs go green while ingesting nothing — exactly the reported experience.
improvements.proposed: (1) Add a structured per-source health counter: in WorkerEngine._run_task, after a task completes, record (source_type, attempted_fetches, http_404, http_5xx, bytes, docs_emitted) into a new state table source_health (or get_metrics()). Increment fetch-outcome counters inside each adapter (pass a small HealthSink via AdapterContext.extras, or return counts in context.extras['health']). (2) Add CLI `awareness sources health` + an API /sources/health endpoint that prints, per source, last-run fetch success rate and docs/fetch. (3) In planner.status() and the backfill summary table, add a warning line when a source completed all tasks with 0 docs AND >0 fetch failures: 'CC-WET: 12/12 tasks ok but 100% of fetches 404 — likely invalid crawl ids or offline'. (4) Emit a one-time WARN ('source_yielded_zero_with_failures') so logs make the failure mode obvious.
improvements.rationale: Silent success on network failure is the defining symptom of 'no idea how to scrape'. Making zero-yield-with-failures a first-class, surfaced state converts invisible failures into actionable signals and prevents regressions like the crawl-id bug from hiding.
improvements.expected_impact: Users immediately see which sources are dead vs merely empty; debugging ingestion goes from guesswork to a single health view. Also gives the team a regression tripwire.

improvements.title: Add a shared HTTP client with timeouts, retries, and exponential backoff (incl. 429/503/Retry-After)
improvements.area: new src/awareness/util/http.py; refactor httpx usage in tail_recrawl.py, commoncrawl_wet.py, cc_index.py, gdelt.py, warc_repair.py, feeds.py, robots.py
improvements.current_state: Every adapter constructs its own `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=…)` per call with no retry. Transient failures behave two ways, both bad: (a) for plain GETs that raise httpx.HTTPError the task dead-letters/retries via state.fail_task but with NO backoff (immediately re-claimed by claim_pending_tasks), and (b) for non-200 responses the adapter returns success with 0 docs and never retries. There is no handling of 429/503 Retry-After, connection resets, or partial timeouts — so a single rate-limit or blip drops a whole shard/slot.
improvements.proposed: Create util/http.py exposing async get_with_retries(client, url, *, max_attempts=settings.max_retries, base_delay=0.5, max_delay=30, retry_status={429,500,502,503,504}, respect_retry_after=True) implementing full-jitter exponential backoff: delay = min(max_delay, base_delay*2**attempt) * random.uniform(0.5,1.0); on 429/503 honor Retry-After header (seconds or HTTP-date) if larger. Use a module-level shared httpx.AsyncClient with httpx.Limits(max_connections=settings.global_fetch_concurrency, max_keepalive_connections=…), http2=True, and a connect/read/write/pool timeout split (httpx.Timeout(connect=10, read=settings.request_timeout_sec, …)). Route the WET/WARC streaming downloads, CDX streaming, GDELT zip, RSS/sitemap, and robots fetches through it (preserving tail_recrawl's explicit per-hop is_public_http_url redirect validation). Distinguish retryable network/5xx/429 (raise -> task requeues with backoff) from terminal 404 (treat as definitive 'not published yet/never', no retry but recorded in source_health).
improvements.rationale: Polite, resilient HTTP with backoff is table stakes for scraping at scale; CC/GDELT/news sites routinely return 429/503 and reset connections. Per-call clients also waste connection setup and defeat keep-alive/HTTP2 pooling.
improvements.expected_impact: Far fewer spurious dead-letters and dropped shards; CC/news fetches survive rate limits and blips; throughput improves via connection reuse. Directly addresses the requested 'real HTTP fetch with retries/timeouts'.

improvements.title: Stop the CLI search from hiding all backfill data behind a 30-day fetch_ts window
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (search cmd line 2595; browse cmd line 2460); align with src/awareness/api/server.py /search (no default window)
improvements.current_state: CLI `search` defaults to --start '30 days ago' and filters base_filters() on `fetch_ts >= start`. But fetch_ts is the ORIGINAL capture date: CC-WET/WARC use the WARC-Date (months/years old), FineWeb uses the row's crawl date, only RSS tail uses ~now. So any historical corpus is invisible to CLI search by default, while the SPA /search (start defaults to None) searches everything. With the default RSS-only corpus being tiny and headline-heavy, a query like 'bitcoin' realistically matches only the couple of recent feed items whose title/snippet contain the word — explaining 'bitcoin returned only 2 results'.
improvements.proposed: (1) Change the CLI search/browse default to no time window (start=None,end=None) like the API, OR default the window to observed_ts (ingest time, always recent) rather than fetch_ts. (2) If a window is desired, make the filter column configurable (--time-field fetch|observed|published, default observed) and apply the same in DuckDbIndex.search base_filters(). (3) Print the active window + field in the results header so an empty result is explained ('0 results in fetch_ts window 2026-05-09..now; try --start all or --time-field observed'). (4) When total==0 and a window was applied, auto-hint to retry with --start all.
improvements.rationale: Search defaults must not silently exclude the bulk of the corpus on a column whose semantics (original capture date) are unrelated to recency of ingestion. The CLI/API divergence is a latent bug.
improvements.expected_impact: 'bitcoin' and similar queries surface the full ingested corpus, not just last-30-day feed headlines. Removes the most visible 'search is broken/janky' symptom.

improvements.title: Add seed discovery: robots.txt Sitemap: directives and /sitemap.xml probing from a bare domain
improvements.area: new src/awareness/sources/discovery.py; src/awareness/sources/feeds.py (_read_sitemap depth); planner.submit_backfill / tail seeds; CLI tail start / backfill --domain
improvements.current_state: Sitemaps must be hand-listed in tail_seeds.yaml (sitemaps: [] by default) and feeds are a fixed curated RSS list. There is no path from 'I care about example.com' to actually crawling it: the CC-Index domain path needs valid crawl ids (currently broken) and the tail path needs a pre-known feed/sitemap URL. _read_sitemap also only follows depth=1 of nested sitemap indexes, so large sites (which nest 2-3 levels) are under-discovered.
improvements.proposed: Add discover_seeds(domain, user_agent): (1) GET https://domain/robots.txt, parse all `Sitemap:` lines (RFC 9309) — this is the canonical sitemap location for most large sites. (2) Fallback-probe common paths: /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml. (3) Probe common feed paths /feed, /rss, /rss.xml, /atom.xml, and parse <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml> from the homepage HTML. (4) Return discovered feed+sitemap URLs and enqueue them as RSS/sitemap partitions. Wire a CLI `awareness discover <domain>` and make `backfill --domain X` / `tail start --domain X` auto-run discovery so a bare domain produces crawl work without CC. (5) Increase _read_sitemap default depth to 3 (bounded) and cap total URLs per sitemap (e.g. 50k) to avoid runaway expansion.
improvements.rationale: A fresh user's mental model is 'point it at a site/topic and it scrapes'. robots.txt Sitemap: + homepage feed autodiscovery is the standard, polite way to bootstrap coverage of an arbitrary domain without depending on Common Crawl latency or a curated feed list.
improvements.expected_impact: Turns 'awareness …  example.com' into real fetched content via sitemaps/feeds within seconds, independent of CC. Dramatically lowers the cold-start barrier and broadens coverage beyond the 30 hardcoded feeds.

improvements.title: Make FineWeb either work out-of-the-box or fail loudly instead of silently no-opping
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/fineweb.py (plan/run_partition); pyproject.toml [hf] extra; planner.submit_backfill default sources
improvements.current_state: FineWeb is in the default backfill source set (planner defaults: COMMON_CRAWL_WET, FINEWEB, GDELT) but the `datasets` package is an optional 'hf' extra and is NOT installed in the project venv (verified: import datasets fails). plan() catches ImportError and returns [] with only an info-level 'fineweb_skipped_missing_datasets_lib' log; run_partition does the same. So one of the three default sources is a guaranteed silent no-op for a default install, and its dump= names would be invalid anyway (see crawl-id bug).
improvements.proposed: Pick one coherent behavior: (A) Remove FINEWEB from the default source set so defaults only include sources that work without extras (CC-WET + GDELT), and document `pip install awareness[hf]` to enable it; OR (B) include datasets in the base deps. Recommended: (A) plus, when a user explicitly requests --source fineweb without datasets installed, RAISE a clear error at submit time ('FineWeb requires the hf extra: pip install awareness[hf]') instead of submitting a job that does nothing. Also make plan() emit a WARNING (not info) and record it in source_health so the no-op is visible. Once crawl-id resolution is fixed, validate dump= against the FineWeb dataset's known config names.
improvements.rationale: A default source that is structurally guaranteed to produce nothing on a default install is a major contributor to 'ingests no data'. Defaults should be honest about what is actually runnable.
improvements.expected_impact: Default backfills stop wasting a third of their planned sources on a no-op; users who want FineWeb get an actionable install hint instead of silent emptiness.

improvements.title: Don't discard short news/feed articles via the global text_min_chars=200 gate
improvements.area: src/awareness/config (text_min_chars default 200); src/awareness/normalize/text.py normalize_text; applied in tail_recrawl via html_to_text and in cc_wet/fineweb normalize_text
improvements.current_state: text_min_chars defaults to 200 and normalize_text discards anything shorter (discarded_reason set -> capture dropped). Many legitimate RSS-sourced articles, breaking-news stubs, and link posts (HN, arXiv abstracts truncated, wire snippets) extract to <200 chars of body, so the live tail — the path most likely to produce a fresh user's first data — silently drops a meaningful fraction of fetched pages. Combined with a small corpus this thins search results further.
improvements.proposed: (1) Lower the default text_min_chars to ~120, or make it source-aware: a smaller floor (e.g. 80) for tail_recrawl/RSS and the current 200 for bulk CC/FineWeb where short records are usually boilerplate. Thread a min_chars override from the adapter into html_to_text/normalize_text. (2) Count drops by reason in source_health ('text_too_short') so the tradeoff is observable. (3) Consider keeping title-only captures for very short bodies when a title exists, marked low-quality, rather than dropping entirely.
improvements.rationale: A one-size 200-char floor optimized for bulk corpora over-prunes the live/news path where short-but-real articles are common, reducing both ingestion volume and searchable diversity.
improvements.expected_impact: Higher capture yield from feeds/tail (the fresh-user path), more search hits per query, fewer 'I fetched it but nothing was saved' surprises.

improvements.title: Move the blocking getaddrinfo SSRF check off the event loop and cache results
improvements.area: src/awareness/util/urls.py (is_public_http_url); callers tail_recrawl._get_public_url, robots._get_public_robots_url
improvements.current_state: is_public_http_url() calls socket.getaddrinfo() synchronously. It is invoked from async fetch paths (tail_recrawl on the initial URL and on EVERY redirect hop, plus robots) — a blocking DNS resolution inside the asyncio event loop. Under the default worker_concurrency=4 / per-domain limits this stalls the loop on slow/มissing DNS and serializes what should be concurrent fetches, throttling the live tail throughput (and any future higher concurrency).
improvements.proposed: (1) Wrap the resolution in loop.run_in_executor (or use an async resolver) so the event loop isn't blocked; expose an async is_public_http_url_async used by the fetch paths, keeping the sync version for non-async callers. (2) Add a small TTL DNS cache (host -> (is_global, expires)) so repeated hits to the same domain (common in tail) don't re-resolve every redirect/page. (3) Bound resolution with a timeout (e.g. 5s) so a hanging resolver can't stall a worker. Keep the existing per-hop public-IP validation semantics intact (SSRF protection must not regress).
improvements.rationale: Blocking DNS in the event loop is a classic asyncio throughput killer and silently caps concurrency; it compounds the 'slow/janky' feel and limits how fast the tail can ingest.
improvements.expected_impact: Higher effective fetch concurrency and a more responsive tail; no SSRF regression. Enables raising global_fetch_concurrency meaningfully.

improvements.title: Make search rank well by default: ensure FTS index builds and prefix-fallback covers multi-term queries
improvements.area: src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (_ensure_fts, search auto/prefix paths, _stem_roots)
improvements.current_state: search 'auto' runs BM25 FTS first and only falls back to stem-prefix if FTS returns 0. FTS requires the optional duckdb 'fts' extension (INSTALL fts at connect, best-effort) and rebuilds captures_idx whenever COUNT(*) changes — on a JSON-backed view this COUNT scan and full CREATE TABLE AS rebuild runs on the query path and can be slow/janky for the user. The prefix fallback ANDs every token's stem-root across fields (where.insert per root), so a 2-word query requires BOTH tokens present, narrowing recall; and FTS is bypassed entirely whenever --fields isn't exactly the default title,text. Together these make ranking inconsistent ('janky in many places').
improvements.proposed: (1) Build/refresh the FTS index out of band (after each flush in WorkerEngine, or on a lightweight timer) rather than lazily on the first query, and gate rebuild on the cheap source-file signature already tracked (_views_signature) instead of a COUNT(*) scan over the JSON view. (2) In the prefix fallback, default to OR across tokens (any token matches) with results ranked by number of matching tokens, so multi-word queries don't collapse recall; keep AND only when match_all is requested. (3) Allow the FTS path to run for field subsets that are a subset of {title,text} by post-filtering, and clearly report used_mode so the UI can show why a query was unranked. (4) Add a tiny BM25 sanity test over a seeded corpus asserting 'bitcoin' ranks a body-mention doc above a title-only unrelated doc.
improvements.rationale: Ranked, low-latency search that degrades gracefully is what makes search feel correct. Lazy index builds on the hot path and AND-only prefix fallback are concrete causes of inconsistent/empty results.
improvements.expected_impact: Consistent BM25 ranking, faster repeat queries, higher recall on multi-word queries; removes the 'search is broken/janky' perception even on a modest corpus.

improvements.title: Provide a one-command 'get me data now' default that actually fetches without flags
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (new quickstart/ingest command); planner.submit_backfill; tail engine
improvements.current_state: To get any data a user must either (a) run a backfill whose default sources are currently broken (CC-WET invalid ids, FineWeb no-op) — leaving GDELT as the only working default, but GDELT backfill is capped to 8 slots (request.max_tasks or 8) and only runs when a tail with --gdelt is started for live; or (b) hand-run `tail start` against the curated feeds. There is no single obvious 'just work' entry point, so a fresh user easily ends up with an empty corpus and the 'bitcoin -> 2 results' experience.
improvements.proposed: Add `awareness quickstart` (and/or make bare `awareness ingest <topic?>` do this): immediately (1) start a short tail over the bundled feeds AND a GDELT slot so docs appear within seconds, (2) kick a small CC-WET backfill over the most recent VALID crawl (using the fixed catalog resolver, max 1-2 shards) for historical depth, (3) print live capture lines and a final 'ingested N docs; try: awareness search "<topic>"'. Respect an optional topic --match to scope it. Ensure non-interactive mode picks safe local sinks. Document this as THE first command in the banner/intro.
improvements.rationale: The fastest way to disprove 'has no idea how to scrape' is a single command that visibly fetches real pages and ends with a working search. It also exercises the fixed CC resolver + working GDELT/feeds end-to-end.
improvements.expected_impact: A fresh user gets a non-empty, searchable corpus in one command and one minute, directly countering both reported symptoms.

improvements.title: CLI search defaults to a 30-day fetch_ts window that hides almost the entire corpus
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (search cmd, lines 2595-2596, 2629-2630, 2639-2640); src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (base_filters, lines 439-444); src/awareness/api/server.py (/search has no such default)
improvements.current_state: `awareness search` sets `--start` default to '30 days ago' and `--end` to 'now', and passes them straight into `DuckDbIndex.search`, which ANDs `fetch_ts >= $start AND fetch_ts <= $end` onto every query. But `fetch_ts` is the ORIGINAL crawl/publish time of the document, not ingest time: CC WET sets it from `WARC-Date`, FineWeb from the row `date`, GDELT-discovered pages from the article. A corpus ingested today from CC-MAIN-2024-26 or FineWeb has fetch_ts months-to-years old, so a 30-day window filters out essentially everything. This is the most likely cause of 'bitcoin returned only 2 results' (the 2 hits are recent RSS/tail captures whose fetch_ts == observed_ts).
improvements.proposed: 1) Change the search default window to be effectively unbounded: default `--start` to None (no lower bound) or 'all'/'1970-01-01', and only apply a fetch_ts filter when the user explicitly passes one. 2) Filter search on `observed_ts` (ingest time) rather than `fetch_ts` for the relevance window, OR expose a `--time-field {fetch_ts,observed_ts}` flag defaulting to observed_ts. 3) In `base_filters()`, skip the range predicate entirely when start/end are None (already the case) and make the CLI pass None by default. Add a one-line result footer when a time filter is active: 'N results in window; M total ignoring date — widen with --start all'.
improvements.rationale: The window is silently intersecting an ingest-time assumption (last 30 days) with a content-time column (fetch_ts) that is almost never in that window for bulk corpora. Users perceive this as 'search is broken' because the data is present (visible via /captures with no date filter) but search returns near-zero.
improvements.expected_impact: Directly fixes the headline symptom: 'bitcoin' (and every other query) will match the full corpus instead of only the last 30 days of content-dated docs. Likely turns 2 results into the true count.

improvements.title: FineWeb/FineWeb2 adapter is a silent no-op because the `datasets` package is not installed
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/fineweb.py (plan lines 56-60, run_partition lines 94-98); pyproject.toml dependency set; src/awareness/planner/planner.py default sources (lines 56-61)
improvements.current_state: `FineWebAdapter.plan()` does `try: import datasets except ImportError: log.info('fineweb_skipped_missing_datasets_lib'); return []`. I verified `datasets` is NOT installed in the project venv (ModuleNotFoundError). FineWeb is one of the 3 default backfill sources, so every default backfill silently emits ZERO FineWeb tasks with only an INFO log. There is no surfaced warning to the operator.
improvements.proposed: 1) Either add `datasets` (and `pyarrow`) to the core dependencies in pyproject.toml, or define an extra `[project.optional-dependencies] fineweb = ["datasets>=2.19"]` and document it. 2) Upgrade the swallow from `log.info` to a `log.warning` AND a metric `inc('fineweb.skipped_no_datasets_lib')`, and have the planner record a job note ('fineweb skipped: datasets lib missing') so the user sees it in `status`. 3) In `submit_backfill`, if a requested/default source produced zero tasks, attach that to the job notes rather than silently dropping it. Also fix `load_dataset(ds_name, name=dump, ...)`: for HuggingFaceFW/fineweb the dump is selected via the `data_dir`/`name` config of that specific dataset; validate the dump arg against the dataset's configs or fall back to the default config when `dump` is not a valid HF config name, else the load raises and is swallowed at lines 112-114.
improvements.rationale: A core ingestion tier is completely inert and the failure is invisible. This is a direct contributor to 'the app has no idea how to scrape the internet' — a third of the default discovery surface produces nothing.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores FineWeb as a working bulk-text source (millions of rows) and makes any future missing-dependency failure loud instead of silent.

improvements.title: Common Crawl WET defaults to 1 shard per crawl, ingesting a trivial fraction of the web
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py (CommonCrawlWetAdapter.__init__ default max_shards_per_crawl=1, lines 100-104; _run_discovery chosen=shards[:max_shards], lines 173-174); src/awareness/config/settings.py
improvements.current_state: The adapter hardcodes `max_shards_per_crawl=1` (comment: 'for sanity in smoke tests') and discovery enqueues only `shards[:1]`. A CC-MAIN crawl has ~90,000 WET shards; ingesting 1 shard per crawl yields ~30-50k docs out of ~3 billion. There is no config knob plumbed to raise it — the only override paths mentioned (notes payload / per-partition) are not wired in plan(). So a default backfill captures an essentially random 0.001% slice, which for a specific term like 'bitcoin' will usually be near-zero.
improvements.proposed: 1) Add `cc_wet_max_shards_per_crawl: int = 50` (or similar) to Settings and read it in the adapter's `plan()`/discovery instead of the constructor constant. 2) Plumb a per-request override via `BackfillRequest` (e.g. `max_shards_per_crawl` or reuse `max_tasks` proportionally). 3) Log the discovered-vs-chosen shard counts at WARNING when chosen << discovered so the operator knows coverage is capped. 4) Optionally distribute shard selection (e.g. evenly sample across the 90k shards) rather than always the first N, to avoid alphabetical-prefix domain bias.
improvements.rationale: The default makes the corpus statistically empty for any specific query. Combined with the date-window bug and FineWeb no-op, the 'body' backfill is effectively non-functional for real research queries.
improvements.expected_impact: Raises CC WET coverage by 1-2 orders of magnitude, making term-specific searches like 'bitcoin' return meaningful counts. Directly addresses the scraping-effectiveness complaint.

improvements.title: Near-dup folding splits clusters: a NEW doc folded under B still anchors its own content_hash group
improvements.area: src/awareness/dedup/engine.py (evaluate, lines 59-106); src/awareness/storage/state.py (upsert_dedup lines 627-637, find_near_dup_candidates lines 663-683)
improvements.current_state: In `evaluate`, step 1 calls `upsert_dedup(content_hash, doc_id)` which for a brand-new content_hash stores `first_doc_id = doc_id (A)` and returns was_new=True. Step 2 then may find a near-dup B and set `cap.parent_doc_or_dup_group = B`. But the `dedup_content` row for A's hash permanently records first_doc_id = A. A later EXACT capture of A's content (same content_hash, e.g. re-crawled) calls upsert_dedup, gets canonical_doc_id = A (not B), and is filed under group A. Result: the near-dup cluster is split into group B (the original near-dup fold) and group A (later exact recaptures), so `WHERE parent_doc_or_dup_group = ?` and the /related view under-count cluster members. Folding is also order-dependent and non-transitive (A~B, B~C does not unify A and C).
improvements.proposed: 1) When a NEW doc is folded as NEAR_DUP under B, update the dedup_content row so A's content_hash maps to B as canonical (i.e. after deciding NEAR_DUP, call a `set_canonical(content_hash_A, B)` so future exact dups of A also resolve to B). 2) Or adopt union-find / connected-components semantics: store a `group_id` and path-compress so A~B and B~C collapse to one root. 3) Persist the chosen `near_dup_hash`/sig so re-evaluation is deterministic. Add an invariant test: ingest A, then B (near-dup of A), then A again, assert all three share one parent group.
improvements.rationale: Dedup is supposed to 'fold not drop' for provenance, but the fold key is inconsistent between the content-hash table and the simhash fold, so the same logical document lands in two groups depending on arrival order. This corrupts cluster counts, /related, and any 'distinct documents' metric.
improvements.expected_impact: Correct, order-independent cluster membership; accurate dedup-stats and related-capture views; no double-counting of distinct docs.

improvements.title: Unsigned 64-bit simhash overflows DuckDB signed BIGINT and becomes NULL on read
improvements.area: src/awareness/schemas/doc.py (near_dup_hash field, line 113, as_iceberg_row line 166); src/awareness/storage/jsonl.py (_serialize_value writes raw int); src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (TRY_CAST(near_dup_hash AS BIGINT), lines 235, 250); src/awareness/storage/iceberg_schema.py (LongType/int64, lines 55, 98)
improvements.current_state: `simhash64()` returns an UNSIGNED 64-bit int (0..2^64-1). It is stored in `DocCapture.near_dup_hash` and serialized verbatim to JSONL as a JSON number. DuckDB reads it via `TRY_CAST(near_dup_hash AS BIGINT)` (signed 64-bit, max 2^63-1). I verified that any value > 2^63-1 (roughly half of all simhashes) TRY_CASTs to NULL. The Iceberg schema is also signed int64, so PyArrow writes will error or overflow for the high half. The durable provenance fingerprint is therefore lost/NULLed for ~50% of rows.
improvements.proposed: 1) Store the simhash as a fixed-width hex string (16 chars for 64-bit, matching the 128-bit sig_hex convention already used in dedup_near) instead of a signed int — change the schema field to StringType and the DuckDB cast to VARCHAR. 2) Or apply the same signed-fold the state DB uses (`legacy = v - 2^64 if v >= 2^63`) at write time and document that near_dup_hash is a signed reinterpretation, undoing it on read. 3) Add a round-trip test: simhash64 of a high-bit text -> write JSONL -> read via DuckDB -> bit-identical.
improvements.rationale: A durable provenance/fingerprint column is silently corrupted to NULL for half the corpus, defeating its stated purpose and any future near-dup recompute from storage.
improvements.expected_impact: near_dup_hash survives the JSONL/Iceberg/DuckDB round trip for all values; provenance fingerprint is recoverable.

improvements.title: Language filter silently drops every document whose language detection returns None
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py (lines 320-322); src/awareness/sources/fineweb.py (lines 129-131); src/awareness/normalize/text.py (detect_language lines 88-99)
improvements.current_state: In CC WET: `lang = detect_language(...) or None; if languages_filter and lang not in languages_filter: continue`. `detect_language` returns None for any text < 80 chars and on any langdetect failure (and its `except (ImportError, Exception)` swallows ALL errors). So when a user requests `languages=['en']`, every document where detection failed/returned None (short docs, mixed scripts, transient errors) is dropped, even genuinely English ones. I verified lang=None with filter {'en'} -> dropped=True. langdetect is also non-deterministic without its seed except where set.
improvements.proposed: 1) Treat None/unknown language as a pass-through when filtering (keep the doc, tag language=None) instead of dropping — only drop on a CONFIDENT mismatch. 2) Make langdetect deterministic and surface real failures: replace `except (ImportError, Exception)` with `except ImportError` + `except LangDetectException`, and emit a metric on detection failure. 3) Lower/justify the 80-char threshold or fall back to a cheap script/stopword heuristic for short docs. 4) Add a metric `docs.dropped_by_language` so over-drop is observable.
improvements.rationale: A correctness filter is conflating 'detected non-English' with 'could not detect', dropping data that should be kept and doing so invisibly. Bare `except Exception` also hides bugs.
improvements.expected_impact: Stops silent loss of English (and unknown-language) documents under any language-filtered backfill; makes language drops observable.

improvements.title: FTS index rebuild keyed on row COUNT can miss content changes, returning stale/empty search
improvements.area: src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (_ensure_fts lines 307-358, esp. count==self._fts_built_for_count short-circuit line 330; _source_signature lines 111-140)
improvements.current_state: `_ensure_fts` rebuilds the materialized `captures_idx` table + FTS index only when `COUNT(*)` changes (`if count == self._fts_built_for_count: return True`). If the corpus changes without the row count changing (e.g. compaction folds JSONL into Iceberg with the same total, a chunk is replaced, or dedup rewrites), the FTS index silently serves the OLD table. Also, `captures_idx` is a full materialization that drops `domain`/`url` from the indexed columns, so FTS can never match domain/url fields, and `auto` only takes the FTS path when fields == default (title,text) — any `--fields` request bypasses ranking entirely and quietly degrades to ILIKE prefix.
improvements.proposed: 1) Key the FTS rebuild on the same `_views_signature` (path+size+mtime) used for view refresh, not on COUNT(*), so any on-disk change triggers a rebuild. 2) Or store a content hash of capture_ids/max(observed_ts). 3) Document/log when a `--fields` request silently disables ranking, and consider building per-field FTS or including domain/url in the indexed blob. 4) On corpus change, also reset `_fts_built_for_count = -1`.
improvements.rationale: Search can return stale or empty results after the corpus changes by an equal-count delta — a 'janky in many places' symptom. COUNT(*) is not a sufficient change detector.
improvements.expected_impact: FTS reflects the current corpus reliably; fewer mysterious empty/stale searches.

improvements.title: Feed cursor truncation to last 5000 URLs corrupts dedup state and re-emits/loses URLs
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/feeds.py (lines 71-75)
improvements.current_state: The feeds cursor does `merged = last_seen | {canonical_url(u) ...}; context.checkpoint['seen_urls'] = list(list(merged)[-5000:])`. `merged` is a SET, so `list(merged)` has arbitrary, run-to-run-varying order; taking the last 5000 of an unordered set keeps a RANDOM 5000 URLs, not the most recent. On the next poll, previously-seen URLs that fell out of the random window are treated as NEW and re-enqueued for fetch (wasteful, and across many polls effectively unbounded re-fetching), while genuinely new URLs can also be evicted. The 'new_urls' diff is therefore unstable.
improvements.proposed: 1) Track seen URLs as an ordered structure (e.g. a list with append + a set for membership, or a bounded `collections.OrderedDict`/deque of fixed maxlen) and keep the MOST RECENT N by insertion order. 2) Better: persist seen-URL state per feed in the state DB (a small table keyed by (partition_key, canonical_url)) rather than a checkpoint blob, so it is durable and exact. 3) Add a metric for re-emitted-already-seen URLs to detect churn.
improvements.rationale: The dedup cursor is the only thing preventing the tail from re-fetching the same articles forever; basing it on an unordered set slice makes it both lossy and noisy, undermining tail correctness and politeness.
improvements.expected_impact: Stable feed diffing: each new article enqueued once, no random re-fetch storms, bounded memory with correct recency.

improvements.title: URL canonicalization under-normalizes (trailing slash, www, index pages), splitting identity
improvements.area: src/awareness/util/urls.py (canonical_url lines 44-81)
improvements.current_state: `canonical_url` only normalizes path when it equals '/', does not strip trailing slashes on deeper paths, does not unify `www.` vs apex host, does not collapse `/index.html`, and does not lowercase the path. So `https://x.com/a` and `https://x.com/a/`, or `www.x.com/a` and `x.com/a`, produce different canonical URLs -> different `doc_id` (doc_id_for hashes canonical_url+content) -> the same page is treated as two documents and EXACT_DUP folding by content_hash partially papers over it but doc_id identity and domain grouping diverge. This inflates distinct-doc counts and fragments dedup groups.
improvements.proposed: 1) Normalize trailing slash consistently (strip a single trailing slash on non-root paths, or always add one — pick one and document). 2) Optionally strip a leading `www.` from netloc (configurable, since some sites differ). 3) Lowercase only the host (already) but consider percent-encoding normalization (decode unreserved, uppercase hex). 4) Collapse common index filenames is risky — gate behind a flag. Add unit tests covering slash/www/case variants mapping to one canonical form.
improvements.rationale: doc_id identity is built on canonical_url; under-normalization splits a single logical document across multiple doc_ids and domains, double-counting and weakening dedup.
improvements.expected_impact: Tighter document identity, fewer spurious distinct docs, better dedup folding and per-domain counts.

improvements.title: /captures and /inspect 'search' use raw ILIKE that diverges from the real search engine
improvements.area: src/awareness/api/server.py (list_captures search branch lines 364-366; inspect lines 280-311)
improvements.current_state: The `/captures` endpoint implements its own `search` as `(title ILIKE %q% OR text ILIKE %q%)` with the FULL query string as one substring — no tokenization, no stemming, no ranking — while `/search` uses BM25/stem-prefix. So the UI's capture-list filter and the search page give different result sets for the same term (e.g. multi-word queries match in /captures only as an exact contiguous substring), reinforcing 'search is janky in many places'. It also scans `text` with ILIKE on every keystroke with no index.
improvements.proposed: 1) Route `/captures?search=` through `DuckDbIndex.search` (or a shared helper) so tokenization/stemming/ranking are consistent everywhere, returning capture_ids to page. 2) If a cheap substring filter must stay, at least tokenize and AND per-token ILIKE like the prefix path does, and document the difference. 3) Add a test asserting that a given query returns a consistent count across /search and /captures within the same time window.
improvements.rationale: Two different matching semantics for 'search' in the same app produce inconsistent counts and confuse users; the contiguous-substring ILIKE is the weakest possible matcher.
improvements.expected_impact: Consistent, predictable search results across UI surfaces; fewer 'why does this differ' reports.

improvements.title: Ingest-time keyword filter uses strict word boundaries, dropping plurals/possessives/compounds
improvements.area: src/awareness/filters.py (_word_boundary lines 35-45, matches lines 87-93)
improvements.current_state: `TopicFilter` keyword mode wraps each term in `\b...\b`, so a topic filter of 'bitcoin' matches 'bitcoin' but NOT 'bitcoins', 'bitcoin-based', '$bitcoin', or 'r/bitcoin' in many tokenizations. This filter runs at INGEST time and DROPS non-matching docs before storage (worker engine lines 336-339). So a user who ran a topic-filtered backfill/tail for 'bitcoin' silently discarded every article that only said 'bitcoins' or 'Bitcoin's' — permanently reducing what is searchable later. This compounds the '2 results' symptom when the corpus was itself built under a too-strict filter.
improvements.proposed: 1) For keyword mode, match a stem/prefix by default: e.g. `\bbitcoin\w*` (trailing word chars allowed) so plurals/derivations pass, while keeping a leading boundary to avoid 'said'. 2) Or run the same Snowball stemming used in search so ingest-filter and search agree. 3) Make boundary strictness configurable (`whole_word` flag). 4) Log a sample of what was filtered, and the filtered count, so over-dropping is visible (the engine already tracks `_total_docs_filtered`; surface it in job notes).
improvements.rationale: The ingest filter is the most destructive stage (it drops, not folds) and its boundary rule is stricter than users expect, silently shrinking the corpus at capture time in a way that cannot be recovered later.
improvements.expected_impact: Topic-filtered ingests keep morphological variants ('bitcoins', 'Bitcoin's'), so later searches over that corpus find far more; reduces permanent silent loss.

improvements.title: JSONL+Iceberg union can double-count or stale-dup captures across the consistency boundary
improvements.area: src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (captures view UNION ALL + ROW_NUMBER dedup, lines 219-264); src/awareness/workers/engine.py (_flush writes JSONL then Iceberg, lines 443-521)
improvements.current_state: The worker flush writes the SAME rows to JSONL (always, when any sink on) AND to Iceberg. The DuckDB `captures` view UNION ALLs staging JSONL with iceberg_captures and dedups by `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY capture_id ORDER BY fetch_ts DESC)` — but ONLY on the iceberg_ok path. When Iceberg is enabled but `iceberg_ok` is False (extension/view setup failed, logged at INFO and swallowed, line 216-217), the view falls back to staging-only and Iceberg rows are invisible; conversely if JSONL staging is later compacted into Iceberg without removing the JSONL chunk, the same capture_id exists in both and is correctly deduped — UNLESS the de-dup column (capture_id) differs because capture_id embeds observed_ts (a fresh fetch yields a new capture_id for the same doc), so re-captures are NOT folded by this view and inflate counts. Net: counts depend on which sinks succeeded and whether compaction ran, with silent fallbacks.
improvements.proposed: 1) Make the JSONL->Iceberg compaction delete (or mark compacted, already a column) the source JSONL chunk and have the view EXCLUDE compacted chunks, so a capture lives in exactly one layer. 2) Surface `iceberg_ok=False` as a WARNING + status flag, not INFO, so silent Iceberg-invisibility is caught. 3) Document that `captures` counts are per-CAPTURE (not per-doc); provide a canonical per-doc count via `parent_doc_or_dup_group`. 4) Add a consistency check command that compares JSONL row counts, manifest sums, and Iceberg snapshot counts.
improvements.rationale: The same data exists in two stores with a fragile reconciliation that silently changes behavior on partial failure or post-compaction overlap, making counts and search totals non-deterministic.
improvements.expected_impact: Deterministic counts regardless of compaction state and partial sink failures; observable Iceberg outages.

improvements.title: Tail recrawl decodes HTML via httpx .text without honoring declared charset/BOM, corrupting non-UTF8 pages
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/tail_recrawl.py (html = r.text, line 106); src/awareness/normalize/html.py (html_to_text)
improvements.current_state: The tail adapter passes `r.text` (httpx's best-guess decode, which for many sites defaults to the charset in Content-Type or falls back to charset-normalizer heuristics) to trafilatura. For pages served as Windows-1251/Shift-JIS/GBK with a correct HTTP charset, httpx usually handles it, but pages that declare charset ONLY in a `<meta>` tag (common for legacy/CJK sites) get mis-decoded into mojibake, which then passes normalization (NFKC won't fix wrong code page) and is stored as corrupted text — making it unsearchable and polluting dedup hashes.
improvements.proposed: 1) Prefer passing raw bytes to trafilatura (it does its own encoding detection from <meta> and BOM) instead of httpx-decoded text — e.g. `trafilatura.extract(r.content, ...)` or pass `r.content` to a decode step that checks meta charset. 2) When using r.text, set `r.encoding` from a meta-charset sniff when Content-Type lacks one. 3) Add a metric/sample for replacement-char ratio; drop or flag docs above a threshold of U+FFFD.
improvements.rationale: Silent character-set corruption produces garbage text that is stored, hashed (polluting dedup), and never matches searches — a correctness loss invisible until someone reads the doc.
improvements.expected_impact: Correct text for non-UTF8/legacy/CJK pages; cleaner dedup fingerprints; more searchable content.

improvements.title: fetch_ts is overloaded as both 'when crawled' and the primary time pivot, breaking time queries
improvements.area: src/awareness/schemas/doc.py (fetch_ts/observed_ts/published_ts); all adapters set fetch_ts to source crawl/publish time; src/awareness/storage/iceberg_schema.py (partitions by day(fetch_ts)); API/CLI time filters all use fetch_ts
improvements.current_state: `fetch_ts` is set to the ORIGINAL content time by bulk adapters (CC WET WARC-Date, FineWeb row date, even tail sets fetch_ts==observed_ts), while `observed_ts` is the true ingest time. Iceberg PARTITIONS by day(fetch_ts) and ALL user-facing time filters (/search, /captures, /inspect, /counts, CLI) filter on fetch_ts. The consequence: (a) ingesting a 2024 crawl today writes into 2024-dated Iceberg partitions, scattering 'what I ingested today' across years; (b) any 'recent' query on fetch_ts misses freshly-ingested old content (the search-window bug above is a symptom of this conflation).
improvements.proposed: 1) Define and document the semantics: published_ts = content authored time, fetch_ts = when the SOURCE captured it, observed_ts = when WE ingested it. 2) Make observed_ts the default pivot for 'recency'/UI listings and partition Iceberg by day(observed_ts) (or add a second partition) so ingest batches are co-located. 3) Audit every adapter so fetch_ts is the source capture time (CC/FineWeb already do) and never silently equals observed_ts unless truly unknown. 4) Provide both 'content time' and 'ingest time' filters in the API.
improvements.rationale: A single overloaded time column is driving partitioning, recency, and filtering with mutually incompatible meanings, which is the root cause behind the search window failure and confusing time-based listings.
improvements.expected_impact: Coherent time semantics: 'recent' means recently ingested, bulk corpora are searchable immediately, Iceberg partitions align with ingest batches.

improvements.title: Remove the silent 30-day default window from CLI search (root cause of "bitcoin returned only 2 results")
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (search command, line ~2595); contrast with API /search which already defaults to no window
improvements.current_state: `awareness search` declares `start: str = typer.Option("30 days ago", "--start")` and passes it as a hard `fetch_ts >= start` filter. Backfilled Common Crawl/FineWeb captures carry `fetch_ts` = the original crawl/publish date (often months or years old), so the default window hides almost the entire backfilled corpus. Reproduced locally: a 3-document corpus matching 'bitcoin' returns total=1 under the 30-day window vs total=3 with no window — exactly the reported '~2 results' symptom. The web UI does not apply this default, so CLI and SPA disagree.
improvements.proposed: Change the default to no lower bound (search the whole corpus) and make any window opt-in. Concretely: set `--start` default to `""` (None) and `--end` default to `""`; only build the `fetch_ts` filter when the user explicitly passes a value (mirror the API: `start=to_utc(start) if start else None`). Add an `--last 30d|7d|24h` convenience flag that sets the window explicitly. When results are returned, print the effective window in the header (e.g. `(window: all dates)` or `(window: 2024-06-01 → now)`) so the scope is never invisible. Add a regression test asserting that `search('bitcoin')` with no `--start` matches docs whose `fetch_ts` is >30 days old.
improvements.rationale: The single highest-impact UX bug: the tool appears to 'lose' data the user knows they ingested. A silent date filter that defaults to recent-only is actively misleading for an engine whose headline feature is historical backfill.
improvements.expected_impact: Searching a backfilled corpus returns all matching documents instead of only those crawled in the last 30 days; CLI and web search become consistent; eliminates the most-reported symptom.

improvements.title: Fix Common Crawl crawl-id resolution (the ISO-week guess 404s on nearly every real crawl)
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py (`crawl_ids_for_range`, `_iso_year_weeks`); also consumed by src/awareness/sources/fineweb.py
improvements.current_state: `crawl_ids_for_range` builds IDs as `CC-MAIN-{ISO-year}-{odd-ISO-week}` (anchoring every date to the nearest odd ISO week). Common Crawl does NOT publish one crawl per fortnight on odd ISO weeks — it publishes ~monthly with irregular week numbers (2024: weeks 10,18,22,26,30,33,38,42,46,51). Verified over the network: the code's generated IDs for 2024-06-01..14 are `CC-MAIN-2024-21` and `CC-MAIN-2024-23`, both HTTP 404 at data.commoncrawl.org/crawl-data/<id>/wet.paths.gz; the real June crawl `CC-MAIN-2024-26` returns 200. So `_run_discovery` fetches a 404, logs `cc_wet_paths_not_found` at warning level, and returns zero shards — the backfill silently produces nothing. This is the concrete mechanism behind 'the app has no idea how to scrape the internet'.
improvements.proposed: Replace the heuristic with the authoritative crawl index. Fetch and cache `https://index.commoncrawl.org/collinfo.json` (the official list of every crawl with `id` and `name`; each entry's id encodes its time range), parse the published crawl list once per run (cache to `data/cache/cc_collinfo.json` with a TTL), and select crawls whose published date range overlaps `[start,end]`. Fall back to a hard-coded table of known crawl IDs per year if the index fetch fails. Add a unit test that asserts a 2024-06 request resolves to `CC-MAIN-2024-26` (not 2024-21/23), and a smoke test (network-gated) that the resolved `wet.paths.gz` returns 200.
improvements.rationale: No amount of UI polish matters if the primary historical source never fetches. The current mapping is a silent, total no-op for the flagship 'BODY' backfill path on essentially all date ranges.
improvements.expected_impact: Backfill against Common Crawl actually downloads WET shards and emits documents; FineWeb dump alignment (which reuses this function) also lands on real dumps; the headline backfill feature works end to end.

improvements.title: Surface silent network/discovery failures instead of swallowing them as warning-level no-ops
improvements.area: src/awareness/sources/commoncrawl_wet.py, sources/feeds.py, sources/fineweb.py, sources/gdelt.py; workers/engine.py; CLI backfill run summary
improvements.current_state: Every adapter swallows failures and returns silently: CC WET 404 on wet.paths.gz → `logger.warning` + `return`; feed/sitemap fetch errors → `logger.warning` + `return []`; FineWeb missing `datasets` lib → `logger.info('fineweb_skipped_missing_datasets_lib')` + empty plan. The backfill summary table reports docs_emitted/tasks but does not distinguish 'task completed with 0 docs because the URL 404'd' from 'task genuinely had no new content'. A user runs `backfill submit/run`, sees tasks 'completed', 0 docs, and no explanation — the exact 'has no idea how to scrape' experience.
improvements.proposed: Add a structured per-task outcome reason persisted on the task row and aggregated per job: enumerate {SOURCE_404, FETCH_ERROR, DECODE_ERROR, FILTERED_OUT_LANG, FILTERED_OUT_DOMAIN, EMPTY_NO_NEW, DEP_MISSING, OK}. In the CLI `backfill run`/`status` summary and the API `/backfill/{id}`, show a 'Why 0 docs?' breakdown (e.g. 'CC-MAIN-2024-21: source not found (404) — likely an invalid crawl id'). When FineWeb is requested but `datasets` is missing, raise a visible warning in the CLI ('FineWeb selected but the [hf] extra is not installed — run `uv pip install -e .[hf]`') rather than an info-level log. Add a `--strict` flag that fails the job if >50% of tasks end in SOURCE_404/FETCH_ERROR.
improvements.rationale: Silent no-ops are the worst failure mode for a scraper: the user cannot tell ineffective configuration from genuinely empty results. Making the reason visible turns a mystifying dead end into an actionable message.
improvements.expected_impact: Users immediately see why a backfill produced nothing (bad crawl id, missing optional dep, all-filtered, network error) and can fix it; dramatically shortens the fresh-clone-to-first-results loop.

improvements.title: Make multi-word search OR-by-default with relevance ranking (currently every term is required, AND)
improvements.area: src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (`search`, prefix fallback ~lines 503-511; FTS path ~458-488)
improvements.current_state: In the prefix/auto fallback, each query token's stem is inserted as a separate `WHERE (cols ILIKE %root%) AND ...`, so a document must contain ALL terms to match. DuckDB's `match_bm25` is also conjunctive by default (`conjunctive=0` is not set). Reproduced: on a 3-doc corpus, 'bitcoin regulators' and 'bitcoin exchanges' each return total=1 because only one doc contains both words, even though every doc is about bitcoin. Multi-word queries therefore collapse to near-zero results and feel 'broken'.
improvements.proposed: (1) Prefix fallback: join the per-term predicates with OR, then rank by the count of distinct terms matched (a cheap TF proxy): `ORDER BY (CAST(title||' '||text ILIKE %t1% AS INT) + ... ) DESC, fetch_ts DESC`. (2) FTS path: keep BM25 but pass the query so DuckDB scores OR-matches (BM25 already down-ranks docs missing terms), i.e. do not force conjunctive matching; expose an explicit `--all`/`match_all` flag for users who want AND. (3) Document the semantics in `--help` and in the SPA search hint ('any word matches; ranked by relevance'). Add tests asserting 'bitcoin regulators' on the 3-doc corpus returns 3 ranked rows with the both-terms doc first.
improvements.rationale: Users expect web-search OR semantics: typing more words should broaden-then-rank, not shrink to exact co-occurrence. The current AND behavior compounds the date-window bug to make search feel arbitrarily empty.
improvements.expected_impact: Multi-word queries return a useful ranked set instead of 0-2 rows; relevance ordering makes the result list feel like a real search engine.

improvements.title: Stop letting missing JSONL columns silently break ALL search/inspect/counts
improvements.area: src/awareness/storage/duckdb_index.py (`_refresh_views`, the explicit column-list SELECT into the `captures` view; exception only logged at warning level ~line 287)
improvements.current_state: `_refresh_views` builds `staging_captures_raw` via `read_json_auto(..., union_by_name=true)`, which only materializes columns actually present in the JSONL. The downstream `captures` view SELECTs the full canonical column list (`parent_doc_or_dup_group`, `near_dup_hash`, etc.). If any JSONL chunk lacks a field, the view build throws a Binder Error that is caught and logged at warning level only — after which the `captures` view does not exist and EVERY subsequent query ('Table with name captures does not exist') fails. Reproduced locally with minimal JSONL rows: search/inspect/counts all crash. Any schema drift, hand-added file, or older ingest_version silently bricks the query surface.
improvements.proposed: Make the view tolerant of missing columns: instead of a hand-written SELECT list, compute the present columns from the raw view and `COALESCE`/synthesize the canonical schema with explicit `NULL::<type> AS <missing_col>` for any field absent in the data (DuckDB `columns()` / information_schema introspection, or build the SELECT list dynamically from the known DocCapture schema, casting present columns and NULL-filling absent ones). On view-build failure, fall back to a guaranteed-non-empty empty-schema view (already defined for the no-files case) AND raise the error to the caller / show it in the CLI rather than swallowing it. Add a test with a JSONL row missing several canonical fields asserting search still returns rows.
improvements.rationale: A single malformed or partial chunk currently takes down the entire read path with only a warning in a log file the user never opens — catastrophic and invisible. Robust NULL-filling matches the union_by_name intent.
improvements.expected_impact: Search/inspect/counts keep working across schema drift and partial data; no more total query-surface outage from one odd file.

improvements.title: Add a one-command 'scrape now' / guided first-run path from fresh clone to first results
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (new `quickstart`/`scrape` command; banner.render_intro context); README Run section
improvements.current_state: From a fresh clone the path to first data is: `init` → edit `configs/tail_seeds.yaml` (or trust defaults) → `backfill submit` (must know a valid date range and that CC mapping works) → `backfill run JOB_ID` → `search` (which then hides results via the 30-day window). The intro banner shows status chips but offers no single action to produce data. Backfill requires the user to pick dates that happen to map to a real crawl. There is no demo/sample corpus, so a brand-new user with a working network still likely sees an empty dashboard and empty search.
improvements.proposed: Add `awareness quickstart` that: (1) runs `init`; (2) starts the tail against the bundled `tail_seeds.yaml` for ~60s (live RSS is the fastest reliable way to get real public text without depending on CC crawl-id correctness), reporting docs captured as they land; (3) prints the exact next commands (`awareness search <term>`, `awareness start` for the dashboard). Also ship `awareness backfill submit --demo` that auto-selects a known-good recent Common Crawl crawl id (post-fix) or, failing network, loads the `local_fixture` source so `search` always has something to find. Update the intro banner to show a prominent 'Run `awareness quickstart` to capture your first documents' call-to-action when `docs == 0`.
improvements.rationale: The README promises a polished end-to-end experience, but the current happy path has several places to stall (crawl-id mapping, date windows, seed editing). A single guaranteed-to-produce-data command is the difference between 'this works' and 'this is broken'.
improvements.expected_impact: A new user goes from clone to visible captures and a successful search in one command, without needing to understand crawl ids or date windows.

improvements.title: Make the SPA Settings page do what the README screenshot promises (editable config, not a read-only dump)
improvements.area: src/awareness/api/web/index.html (settings view ~line 362), web/app.js (`loadSettings` ~line 792), src/awareness/api/server.py (no settings GET/PATCH endpoints)
improvements.current_state: The README's Settings screenshot caption promises 'backfill submission form, source toggles, language filters, project / data directory paths'. The actual Settings view (`loadSettings`) only renders read-only key/value rows from `/healthz` and `/dedup-stats`; the lede even says 'read-only from the UI'. The backfill form actually lives on the Jobs page. There is no UI to toggle sources, set languages, change data dir, or edit `tail_poll_seconds` — and no API to read/write the YAML config (the CLI has `config get/set` but the SPA can't reach it).
improvements.proposed: Add `GET /config` and `PATCH /config` endpoints backed by the existing `config set/unset` YAML logic (whitelist editable keys: search_default_mode/fields/limit, tail_poll_seconds, enable_iceberg, per_domain_concurrency, user_agent, languages, data_dir-display). In the Settings view render editable controls (selects/toggles/number inputs) bound to those keys with a Save button that PATCHes and toasts success; show current effective value plus its source (yaml vs env vs default). Add the tail seed list (read from `/tail/status` per_seed) with an 'edit configs/tail_seeds.yaml' affordance. Either implement the promised controls or correct the README caption — implementing is preferred for completeness.
improvements.rationale: A headline screenshot describing functionality that doesn't exist is a credibility and usability gap; users navigate to Settings expecting to change behavior and find a static dump.
improvements.expected_impact: Settings becomes a real control surface (matching the docs), letting users tune search/tail behavior without dropping to the CLI or hand-editing YAML.

improvements.title: Improve search empty-states and tell the user WHY a search returned nothing
improvements.area: src/awareness/cli/main.py (search command output ~2691-2698), web/app.js (`loadCaptures` meta ~315-327)
improvements.current_state: On zero results the CLI prints only `No documents matched query '<q>'.` and the SPA shows `0–0 of 0 matches · <mode>`. Neither tells the user that a date window is in effect, that multi-word AND semantics may be the cause, that the corpus itself is empty, or that the term exists but outside the window. There is no 'did you mean / try broadening' guidance, and no indication whether 0 results means 'no data ingested yet' vs 'data exists but nothing matched'.
improvements.proposed: When a search returns 0 rows: (1) run a cheap `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM captures` (respecting only source/domain, not the query/date) — if the corpus is empty, show 'No documents ingested yet — run `awareness quickstart` or a backfill' (CLI) / link to the backfill form (SPA); (2) if the corpus is non-empty but the windowed query matched nothing, re-run the same query with the date window removed and, if it now matches, surface 'N matches exist outside your date window [<start>..<end>] — broaden with --start or clear the date filter'; (3) if multiple terms were ANDed, suggest 'try fewer words or --any'. Show the active mode/fields/window inline on every result header, not just on zero.
improvements.rationale: Distinguishing 'empty corpus' from 'over-filtered query' is the difference between a confused user and a self-correcting one; it directly addresses 'search is janky in many places'.
improvements.expected_impact: Zero-result searches become self-explanatory and recoverable; users learn the date/term controls instead of concluding the tool is broken.

improvements.title: Expose and unify search mode/fields across CLI, API, and SPA so behavior is predictable
improvements.area: src/awareness/api/server.py (/search and /captures search branch), web/app.js (loadCaptures builds /search without mode), src/awareness/cli/main.py (search)
improvements.current_state: Three search surfaces disagree. CLI `search` supports `--mode` and `--fields` and a 30-day default window. API `/search` accepts mode/fields but the SPA's `loadCaptures` never sends them (always config default) and never sends a window unless the user picks dates. The `/captures` endpoint has its own separate `search` param doing a raw `title ILIKE %q% OR text ILIKE %q%` (a 4th, unranked, substring behavior) used when... actually it is shadowed because the SPA routes any `q` to `/search`. So `/captures?search=` is dead code, and users get different ranking/semantics depending on surface.
improvements.proposed: Pick one search contract. Route all UI/CLI search through `idx.search()` with explicit `mode`/`fields`/window params surfaced in each UI: add a mode selector (auto/fts/prefix/substring) and a fields multiselect to the SPA captures toolbar, defaulting from `/config`. Remove or redirect the redundant `/captures?search=` substring branch to `/search` to avoid a divergent code path. Ensure the SPA shows the resolved `mode`/`ranked` it got back (it already reads `data.ranked`) and the effective window. Document the one contract in the README.
improvements.rationale: Inconsistent search semantics across surfaces is a core reason it feels 'janky in many places' — the same query yields different counts/orderings depending on where you type it.
improvements.expected_impact: One predictable, controllable search behavior everywhere; removes dead/divergent code paths; users can reason about why results differ.

improvements.title: Cap discovery fan-out and make default GDELT/CC shard volume sane so first backfills finish quickly and visibly
improvements.area: src/awareness/planner/planner.py (max_tasks only caps initial output), workers/engine.py (sub-partition enqueue), sources/commoncrawl_wet.py (max_shards_per_crawl=1), sources/gdelt.py
improvements.current_state: README itself warns: `max_tasks` caps only the planner's initial output; sub-partitions from discovery (CC index→WARC repair, GDELT slot→tail recrawl, CC discovery→shard fetch) are uncapped — 'a single GDELT 15-minute slot can fan out into 1000+ sub-fetches.' Meanwhile CC WET defaults to `max_shards_per_crawl=1` (one ~100-500 MB shard). So a default backfill is simultaneously at risk of unbounded fan-out (GDELT/index path) and too-small a sample (1 WET shard) — a confusing mix where a 'quick' run either does almost nothing or explodes.
improvements.proposed: Add a single `--budget` concept (max total documents OR max total sub-tasks) that the worker enforces across the WHOLE job including discovery-enqueued sub-partitions, not just the planner. Plumb a per-job counter through `enqueue_subpartitions` so once the budget is hit, further discovery enqueues are dropped with a 'budget reached' task outcome (ties into surface-ingestion-noops). Set conservative, finishing-in-minutes defaults for first runs (e.g. budget=2000 docs) and document raising it. Show 'X / budget documents' progress in the CLI run summary and SPA job row.
improvements.rationale: Predictable, bounded, visibly-progressing runs are essential for trust; the current uncapped-vs-tiny-sample split makes the engine feel either inert or runaway, undermining the 'single laptop process' promise.
improvements.expected_impact: Default backfills complete in a bounded time with a clear progress denominator; no surprise 1000-task fan-outs; users can dial volume up deliberately.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Stop the bleeding: fix all verified bugs
phases.goal: Eliminate every confirmed correctness/crash bug, ordered by severity then dependency. These are deviations from intended behavior that produce crashes, silent data loss, or wrong results regardless of any new feature work. Land the crash/data-loss fixes first (orchestration), then the search-window and date-filter correctness bugs that directly cause the 'bitcoin returned 2 results' symptom, then the medium/low UX defects.

items.title: Import JobStatus in tail/engine.py (one-line fix; crashes `tail start --job-id` resume path)
items.why: Deterministic NameError crash on the documented resume flow. Trivial fix (add JobStatus to line 29 import), no dependencies. Dedup of duplicate bug entries tail-engine-jobstatus-nameerror and tail-engine-jobstatus-nameerror-on-resume.

items.title: Make claim_pending_tasks atomic against cross-process double-claim
items.why: Two worker processes (standalone awareness-worker + API/CLI) double-claim the same task → duplicate fetches, duplicate captures, corrupted counters. Must use a DB-level atomic UPDATE (SQLite LIMIT-by-subquery / Postgres RETURNING) plus a job-already-RUNNING guard on /backfill/{id}/run. In-process async is NOT the trigger; the cross-process race is.

items.title: Add startup/periodic reaper to reset orphaned RUNNING tasks to PENDING
items.why: Crash/kill mid-task strands backfill tasks in RUNNING forever (no reaper, no lease). Permanent silent corpus loss for backfill jobs. Add a lease/started_at-based reset respecting max_retries.

items.title: Don't mark job COMPLETED on graceful stop with PENDING/RUNNING tasks remaining
items.why: Ctrl-C/SIGTERM marks job COMPLETED even with unprocessed tasks; resume skips COMPLETED jobs so work is lost. Only set COMPLETED when queue drained AND not is_stopping(); leave RUNNING/PAUSED otherwise. Pairs with the reaper fix.

items.title: Remove the 30-day default fetch_ts window from CLI search and browse
items.why: Highest-probability cause of the user's 'bitcoin → 2 results' report. fetch_ts is the original crawl/publish date (months/years old for CC/FineWeb), so the default window hides the entire backfilled corpus while the API searches unbounded. Default --start/--end to None on search (main.py:2595) and browse (main.py:2460). Dedup of cli-search-default-30day-window-hides-results, search-default-30day-window-hides-corpus, search-default-30-day-window-hides-corpus.

items.title: Treat date-only `end` as inclusive end-of-day across /captures, /search, /inspect, /counts
items.why: Bare YYYY-MM-DD end parses to midnight, so `fetch_ts <= end` silently drops the entire selected final day (and From=To=today returns zero). Coerce date-only end to 23:59:59.999999 or use `< end+1day`. Apply to all four endpoints including /counts.

items.title: Index .jsonl.gz chunks (rglob('*.jsonl') misses them)
items.why: With jsonl_compress=True and Iceberg off, the entire staging corpus is invisible to search — total silent search failure for compressed deployments. Glob '*.jsonl*' at duckdb_index.py:122 and :151.

items.title: Distinguish transient HTTP failures from genuine 404s in discovery adapters
items.why: Transient 429/503/timeout from CC/GDELT is swallowed as a bare return → task COMPLETED docs_emitted=0, never retried. Raise on transient/5xx/429 so the existing retry/DLQ path fires; keep 404 'not published' as benign but counted. Dedup with silent-discovery-no-op-empty-corpus (same root, observability framing).

items.title: Declare near_dup_hash as BigInteger (32-bit Integer overflows on Postgres)
items.why: 64-bit simhash written to a 32-bit INTEGER column crashes add_near_dup_index for ~every doc on Postgres (silent on default SQLite). Use BigInteger().with_variant(Integer,'sqlite'), or drop the vestigial column.

items.title: Re-inspect columns after the sig_hex ALTER and raise loudly if still missing
items.why: A swallowed migration failure leaves dedup_near without sig_hex; every near-dup read/write then fails for the whole run behind one warning line. Narrow the except and re-check the column post-ALTER.

items.title: Move blocking getaddrinfo (is_public_http_url) off the event loop
items.why: Synchronous socket.getaddrinfo with no timeout on the async tail path (3 call sites incl. robots.py:32) freezes the whole worker loop on slow/hanging DNS. Wrap in asyncio.to_thread + short-TTL cache + timeout. Dedup with offload-blocking-dns-in-ssrf-check improvement.

items.title: Key FTS rebuild on content signature, not row COUNT
items.why: Count-stable content changes (in-place edits, compaction migrating rows) serve stale BM25 results, including a confidently-ranked phantom hit in default auto mode. Drop the count==_fts_built_for_count early return; use _source_signature() or a (count,max_ts) fingerprint. Dedup of two duplicate entries (fts-index-rebuild-keyed-on-rowcount + fts-index-stale-row-count-signature).

items.title: Unify multi-word semantics: FTS is OR, prefix fallback is AND
items.why: Same query returns different result sets depending on whether FTS is available (OR) vs prefix fallback (AND). Pick one (pass conjunctive:=1 to match_bm25 to make FTS conjunctive, or OR the prefix roots) and document it.

items.title: Fix stem-root substring match missing surface forms (mining→mine)
items.why: In prefix/fallback mode (FTS available + narrowed fields or explicit prefix), Snowball stems that aren't substrings of the surface form (mine vs mining) yield zero matches. OR-in the raw token alongside the stem root.

items.title: Make fts_eligible order-insensitive (set equality, not list equality)
items.why: `--fields text,title` (swapped order, same set) silently drops BM25 ranking. Use set(cols)==set(DEFAULT_SEARCH_FIELDS). NOTE: do NOT change to subset — single-field requests are intentionally ineligible (guarded by test_auto_mode_honors_narrowed_fields).

items.title: Fix snippet/highlight to match the stem roots search actually used
items.why: Prefix/fallback mode attaches stem roots as terms but highlights with `\b(term)\b`, so almost nothing highlights (Snowball truncates every token). Highlight on roots with a prefix-aware pattern; keep server _snippet_for and SPA highlightedFragment consistent. Dedup with highlight-misses-midword-substring-matches.

items.title: Non-interactive search: default limit to max_results and print 'showing N of M'
items.why: Piped search returns only one page (default 10) with no pagination hint. Default limit to max_results in the non-interactive branch and always print 'showing N of M; pass --limit'.

items.title: Fix the dead '(capped)' indicator (len(rows)>=max_results never true)
items.why: Compare against the ceiling (total>=max_results) or return an explicit truncated flag from idx.search. Low effort, folds into the pagination fix.

items.title: Bound-check interactive paging at the last page; use server's clamped offset
items.why: Past offset=max_results the same last page is re-served while the page counter keeps climbing. Bound-check before offset+=limit and read res['offset'] for the label.

items.title: Fix SPA pagination corruption past max_results (offset rewrite + uncapped total)
items.why: Server silently rewrites offset>=max_results to a different window while SPA keeps its own offset and an uncapped total, so Next never disables and stale rows repeat. Return capped total / honor data.offset in app.js.

items.title: Make DuckDbIndex a process-wide singleton (FTS rebuilt on every /search request)
items.why: Per-request instantiation makes the FTS caching dead; every keystroke-debounced /search does a full corpus materialize + BM25 rebuild (16-24x slower, scales with corpus). Build once in lifespan / lru_cache by db_path. Prerequisite for the concurrency-conflict fix below.

items.title: Serialize index rebuilds to stop DuckDB 'Catalog write-write conflict' 500s
items.why: Overlapping /search (and non-FTS endpoints via view rebuild) crash with write-write conflicts on captures_idx/staging_captures_raw. The singleton fix (above) plus a single shared connection+lock resolves both; treat conflict as 'someone else is building' retry.

items.title: Make the captures view resilient to a structurally-missing column
items.why: One JSONL chunk missing a key throws a swallowed BinderException, leaving the captures view undefined so ALL search/inspect/counts/related fail. Latent today (as_iceberg_row writes all 29 fields) but a robustness landmine; COALESCE absent columns to typed NULLs and log the offending file. Dedup with harden-captures-view-against-schema-drift.

items.title: Google Drive upload: read bytes (read_text crashes on .jsonl.gz)
items.why: With jsonl_compress=True, gdrive.upload_file's read_text raises UnicodeDecodeError → permanent silent upload failure. Use read_bytes + octet-stream/gzip Content-Type (mirror cli/main.py:2823's gzip-aware reader).

items.title: Reject unparseable --start instead of silently widening to all-time
items.why: `--start '1 week ago'` parses to None and drops the lower bound (narrowing intent becomes widening). Raise typer.BadParameter on non-empty unparseable input (pattern already exists at main.py:1104-1106).

items.title: Catch ParserError from coerce_relative_end / --end (and query/counts/backfill)
items.why: `--end lastweek` dumps a raw traceback. Harden coerce_relative_end to catch ParserError (match to_utc) and convert to BadParameter at all call sites (search 2630, query 1644, counts 1692, backfill 1111). Dedup with coerce-relative-end-rejects-days-ago.

items.title: Accept 'N days ago' in coerce_relative_end (asymmetry with to_utc)
items.why: `--end 'N days ago'` crashes while `--start 'N days ago'` works; the default --start is literally '30 days ago'. Route coerce_relative_end through to_utc. Folds into the search-end-parse-crash fix.

items.title: Use order-preserving dedup for the feeds seen_urls cursor
items.why: `list(set(...))[-5000:]` keeps an arbitrary 5000, so the cursor never converges for feeds >5000 URLs and re-flags thousands as new each poll. Use dict.fromkeys to preserve insertion order. Network re-fetch is largely prevented by the COMPLETED-task guard (state.py:347-358), so impact is per-poll churn + wrong new-URL metrics. Dedup of two duplicate entries.

items.title: Normalize domain filter through domain_of() in WET and FineWeb
items.why: User passing a subdomain (www.cnn.com, news.bbc.co.uk) matches nothing because the filter compares raw input to eTLD+1. Build domains_filter = {domain_of(d) for d in request.domains} (cc_index already does suffix matching). Lives here as a verified bug; the broader collinfo fix is Phase 2.

items.title: Document/fix that WET (and all adapters) re-parse from record 0 on retry
items.why: No per-record checkpoint; a late failure re-parses the whole cached shard. Real root cause is engine-level (fail_task discards context.checkpoint), so the streaming-generator fix must be paired with persisting checkpoints on the failure path. Bounded by content-hash dedup, so low severity — schedule after the higher-severity items.

items.title: Pass text_min_chars/max_chars into html_to_text in tail_recrawl and warc_repair
items.why: The primary live-scraping path silently ignores the documented corpus-length config. Thread settings through (straightforward in tail_recrawl; needs settings plumbed into warc_repair._parse_warc_record).

items.title: Gate near-dup on a minimum shingle/token count for short docs
items.why: Fixed Hamming<=24 over length-sensitive simhash misses genuine near-dups of short docs (recall loss only — no false merges). Add a minimum-shingle gate so short docs rely on exact content_hash. Quality issue, no data loss; lowest priority in Phase 1. Deeper threshold/banding work is Phase 4.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Make scraping actually work
phases.goal: Fix the ingestion path so a fresh user actually gets real data.
