The dominant root cause ('the app has no idea how to scrape the internet') is fabricated Common Crawl IDs + a 1-shard default + an inert FineWeb source + silent no-ops. Land the crawl-ID fix first (it unblocks WET/CC-Index/FineWeb at once), then breadth, robustness, discovery, and visibility.

items.title: Resolve real crawl IDs from collinfo.json instead of synthesizing odd-week IDs
items.why: Single highest-leverage fix: the odd-week heuristic 404s on most real crawls, so WET/CC-Index/FineWeb all target non-existent crawls and emit ~0 docs. Fetch+cache https://index.commoncrawl.org/collinfo.json, select by overlapping from/to windows, ship a bundled fallback, and fix the unit test to assert IDs intersect a real-crawl set. Dedup of 4 duplicate improvement entries (cc-crawl-id-discovery-from-collinfo, fix-commoncrawl-crawl-id-resolution, fix-commoncrawl-crawl-id-mapping) and bug cc-crawl-id-odd-week-heuristic-wrong.

items.title: Shared HTTP client with timeouts, retries, exp backoff + Retry-After (429/503)
items.why: max_retries/backoff_base_sec are defined but never wired in; every fetch is single-shot and dies on the first hiccup. Add util/http.py with full-jitter backoff, Retry-After honoring, retryable-vs-terminal status classification, and route all adapters through it. Dedup of add-http-retries-backoff-respect-retry-after + http-retry-backoff-transport.

items.title: Make WET shards-per-crawl configurable (default >1) and spread-sample shards
items.why: max_shards_per_crawl=1 is a smoke-test default that ships; one shard is ~0.001% of a crawl, so even a 'successful' backfill yields a topically-random sliver. Plumb from settings/BackfillRequest, raise the default (e.g. 8), and stride-sample instead of shards[:N] to avoid alphabetical-prefix bias. Dedup of expose-cc-wet-shard-count, increase-default-fetch-breadth, ingestion-raise-cc-wet-shard-default-and-config, cc-wet-max-shards-one-tiny-corpus.

items.title: Make FineWeb work out-of-the-box or fail loudly (datasets not installed)
items.why: FineWeb is a default source but `datasets` isn't installed, so a third of default ingestion is a silent INFO-level no-op. Either add the dep / [hf] extra, or remove FINEWEB from defaults and raise a clear error when explicitly requested. Promote the skip to WARNING + job note. Dedup of install-fineweb-deps-or-warn-loudly, surface-ingestion-noops, ingestion-surface-fineweb-missing-datasets, fineweb-silent-noop-no-datasets-dep.

items.title: Surface zero-yield discovery as a health signal, not a green no-op
items.why: Silent success on zero output is the defining symptom. Add per-source health counters (attempted/404/5xx/docs), a 'completed_empty' job state, a CLI 'sources health' / status breakdown, and an actionable hint when the corpus is empty. Dedup of fail-loud-on-empty-discovery, surface-zero-yield-source-health, surface-ingestion-noops-to-user, silent-discovery-no-op-empty-corpus.

items.title: Warn loudly when a backfill plans zero tasks (per-source reasons)
items.why: submit_backfill returns a green job_id even when total_tasks==0 (e.g. CC-index needs --domain, FineWeb dep missing). Set a terminal EMPTY state with enumerated per-source reasons and print a yellow warning instead of green success.

items.title: Seed discovery from robots.txt Sitemap: directives and feed autodiscovery
items.why: There's no path from 'I care about example.com' to crawling it without CC. Parse robots.txt Sitemap: lines, probe common sitemap/feed paths, parse homepage <link rel=alternate>, and increase _read_sitemap depth (bounded). Makes a bare domain produce content within seconds, independent of CC latency.

items.title: Lower/source-aware text_min_chars so short news/feed articles aren't dropped
items.why: The global 200-char floor over-prunes the live tail (the fresh-user path) where legitimate short articles are common. Make it source-aware (smaller floor for tail/RSS) and count drops by reason. Depends on the tail_recrawl min_chars plumbing from Phase 1.

items.title: Fix the per-domain rate limiter so inter-fetch delay holds under concurrency
items.why: acquire reads last_release (only set on release) under a semaphore allowing N holders, so crawl-delay isn't enforced — risking 429s/IP bans that look like 'scraping doesn't work'. Use a per-domain next_allowed_at under a lock + monotonic clock; add the unused global_fetch_concurrency cap.

items.title: Add attempt-bounded, backoff-delayed task retries (next_attempt_at)
items.why: fail_task immediately re-PENDINGs; a fast-failing task burns all max_retries in ~2s and hammers the upstream. Add next_attempt_at with exp backoff+jitter and filter it in claim_pending_tasks. Complements the Phase 2 HTTP retry and Phase 1 atomic-claim fixes.

items.title: One-command 'quickstart' that visibly fetches real data (tail + GDELT + small CC)
items.why: Fastest way to disprove 'has no idea how to scrape': a single command that tails bundled feeds + a GDELT slot + a small CC-WET backfill on a real (post-fix) crawl, ending with a working search. Dedup of sensible-default-backfill-quickstart + first-run-quickstart-and-scrape-now.

items.title: Add a whole-job document/sub-task budget to bound discovery fan-out
items.why: max_tasks caps only initial planner output; a single GDELT slot can fan out into 1000+ sub-fetches while CC defaults to 1 shard — a confusing inert-vs-runaway split. Add a job-wide --budget enforced through enqueue_subpartitions with visible progress.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Search that works
phases.goal: After the corpus is populated and the window/date bugs are fixed (Phase 1), make search behave like a real engine: consistent across CLI/API/SPA, OR-by-default multi-word recall, working FTS, faceting, and capability for phrase/prefix/fuzzy. These are feature/quality improvements layered on the bug fixes.

items.title: Make multi-word search OR-by-default with relevance ranking
items.why: Prefix fallback ANDs every term and match_bm25 defaults conjunctive, so 'bitcoin regulators' collapses to near-zero. OR the prefix predicates ranked by terms-matched, keep BM25 disjunctive, and add an explicit --all flag. Closely tied to the Phase 1 OR-vs-AND consistency fix; this is the chosen direction (OR-default).

items.title: One config-driven resolve_search_params shared by CLI, dashboard, and API
items.why: Defaults are resolved in 3 divergent places (how the 30-day bug existed only on CLI). Centralize mode/fields/window/limit resolution and add a regression test asserting CLI and API return the same total. Dedup of unify-search-defaults-config-driven + unify-search-modes-cli-api.

items.title: Build FTS out-of-band on flush; widen auto-mode coverage
items.why: Lazy FTS build on the query path + AND-only prefix fallback + FTS bypassed for non-default fields make ranking inconsistent and slow. Build/refresh FTS after flush keyed on the file signature, allow FTS for subsets of {title,text}, and report used_mode.

items.title: Graceful, transparent fallback when FTS strips a query (hyphens/operators/phrases)
items.why: match_bm25 silently returns nothing for 'bit-coin', '"phrase"', 'C++' in explicit fts mode. Auto-retry prefix, pre-normalize hyphens, and de-hyphenate joined tokens so punctuated queries never return empty.

items.title: Add phrase, true-prefix (term*), and fuzzy (levenshtein/trigram) modes
items.why: Users type quotes, partial words, and typos; a 'search that works' must degrade gracefully. DuckDB ships levenshtein/jaccard so no new dep. Larger effort, after the core recall/consistency fixes.

items.title: Add facet counts (source/domain/language/time bucket) to search results
items.why: Both UX and diagnostic: '2 results, all 2014, all cc-wet' instantly explains a thin result as a corpus/date issue. Share one predicate CTE so facets and totals stay consistent.

items.title: Route /captures?search= through the real search engine (or remove it)
items.why: /captures uses a raw full-string ILIKE (a 4th divergent matcher) inconsistent with /search. Route through idx.search or remove the dead/divergent branch. Folds into the unify-search-defaults work.

items.title: Explain WHY a search returned nothing (empty corpus vs over-filtered)
items.why: Distinguish 'no data ingested' from 'data exists outside your window/terms', re-run without the window to detect hidden matches, and surface the active mode/fields/window on every result. Turns dead-ends into self-correcting prompts.

items.title: Best-window snippets + stem-aware/multibyte highlighting (shared helper)
items.why: Extends the Phase 1 highlight fix: pick the densest window, highlight on matched roots, and handle CJK/short tokens. Unify CLI and server highlighting through one helper.

items.title: Stable keyset pagination + cache total across page turns
items.why: Deep OFFSET paging is O(offset) and unstable under concurrent writes; recomputing COUNT(*) per page is wasteful. Add a deterministic tiebreaker (score DESC, capture_id ASC), keyset cursors for the recency path, and cache total on page 0.

items.title: Loosen ingest-time keyword filter to stem/prefix (drops plurals today)
items.why: The ingest TopicFilter uses strict \b...\b, so a 'bitcoin' topic backfill permanently discards 'bitcoins'/'Bitcoin's' at capture time — unrecoverable corpus loss feeding the '2 results' symptom. Match stem/prefix (align with search) and make whole-word opt-in. Placed here because it interacts with search semantics, though it's an ingest-side filter.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Mathematical upgrades
phases.goal: Improve the statistical correctness and quality of dedup, ranking, hashing, and benchmarks. These are not bugs but principled upgrades that raise precision/recall and make benchmark claims defensible. Depends on the dedup correctness fixes from Phase 1.

items.title: Make SimHash banding satisfy the pigeonhole guarantee at the real threshold
items.why: 16 bands of 8 bits only guarantees exact retrieval for Hamming<16, but the threshold is 24 — so true near-dups in the 16-24 range are probabilistically missed before the Hamming check. Choose bands from the threshold (Manku multi-probe) and assert engine recall == oracle recall.

items.title: Replace the hand-picked Hamming=24 with an FPR-controlled, calibrated cutoff
items.why: 24 is a narrative constant. Derive T from the Binomial(128,1/2) null at a target false-merge rate and add an `awareness dedup calibrate` command that fits the corpus distance histogram. Depends on the Phase 1 short-doc gate and the banding fix.

items.title: Weight SimHash shingles by corpus IDF (Charikar), not just local count
items.why: Local 1+ln(count) ignores corpus boilerplate ('all rights reserved'), which pollutes signatures of template-identical-but-different pages. Add a streaming DF sketch (Count-Min) and tf-idf weighting; reduces false near-dup merges on CMS-templated corpora.

items.title: Use 128-bit content_hash and tune shingle size k
items.why: 64-bit xxh3 content hash silently merges distinct docs at web scale (~1e-3 collisions at 1e7 docs); xxh3_128 is already used for doc_id and makes this negligible. Also benchmark k in {2..5} (k=4-5 usually maximizes near-dup F1).

items.title: Stop near_dup_hash overflowing DuckDB signed BIGINT to NULL (~50% of rows)
items.why: Unsigned 64-bit simhash > 2^63-1 TRY_CASTs to NULL, losing the durable fingerprint for half the corpus. Store as fixed-width hex (like sig_hex) or apply a signed fold consistently. Complements the Phase 1 Postgres Integer-overflow fix (different store: DuckDB/JSONL/Iceberg vs state DB).

items.title: Make near-dup folding order-independent (union-find / set_canonical)
items.why: A NEW doc folded under B still anchors its own content_hash group, so later exact recaptures file under A — splitting the cluster and corrupting /related and distinct-doc counts. Adopt union-find or update the content_hash→canonical mapping on fold.

items.title: BM25F field-boosted scoring (title weight) + tuned k1/b
items.why: Title and text are one undifferentiated blob; a title hit ranks like a buried body hit. Score title and text separately (w_title≈3), tune k1/b explicitly for web-length variance, add a light recency prior, validate with nDCG@10. Dedup with search-bm25-field-boost-and-recency.

items.title: Fix histogram first-N sampling bias; add reservoir sampling + p50/p95/p99
items.why: _Histogram keeps only the first 256 samples and exposes no percentiles, biasing every latency claim. Use Vitter Algorithm R + numpy.percentile / t-digest. Prerequisite for trustworthy latency reporting in benchmarks and Phase 5 observability.

items.title: Add bootstrap CIs and a real-text holdout to near-dup benchmarks
items.why: Single-seed point estimates on a self-generated corpus overstate precision and risk threshold overfitting. Report mean±95% bootstrap CI, add a real-text validation set, and select the threshold on a disjoint split.

items.title: Confidence-aware LID (fastText lid.176 / CLD3), length gating, trust FineWeb metadata
items.why: langdetect is top-1, no confidence, unstable on short/markup text, and swallows all errors — so language filters wrongly drop/keep docs. Use a calibrated detector with p/len gating, emit 'und' instead of None, and trust upstream FineWeb language. Raises web-text LID accuracy ~0.90→0.98.

items.title: Add Gopher/C4-style content-quality filter to WET extraction
items.why: WET accepts any record passing only min_chars, so nav/cookie/SEO boilerplate pollutes search and dedup signatures. Apply cheap O(n) line-length/symbol-ratio/stopword/duplicate-line heuristics into a quality_score with discarded_reason.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Systems-engineering upgrades
phases.goal: Throughput, memory, storage layout, and observability hardening for a single-process engine at scale. These make the engine fast and operable; they depend on the scraping (Phase 2) and search (Phase 3) paths being correct first.

items.title: Persist captures_idx and update FTS incrementally instead of full rebuild
items.why: Per-query full re-materialize of all JSONL + BM25 rebuild is O(corpus) per search — the search-latency cliff. Persist captures_idx, append only new rows by watermark, and amortize/hot-delta the FTS rebuild. Depends on the Phase 1 singleton + content-signature fixes.

items.title: Stream WET parsing via a bounded queue instead of buffering the whole shard
items.why: _parse_wet_to_captures returns the entire shard as a list of DocCapture objects × worker_concurrency → multi-GB RSS and OOM risk. Stream over a bounded asyncio.Queue (turns the dead bounded_queue_size knob into real backpressure) and lower time-to-first-doc.

items.title: Shared pooled httpx client (keep-alive/HTTP2) + global fetch/extract concurrency
items.why: Every fetch builds a fresh AsyncClient (no pooling, unbounded sockets); global_fetch_concurrency/extract_concurrency are dead config. Inject a process-singleton client via AdapterContext, cap with a global semaphore, and bound CPU-bound extraction in a dedicated executor. Builds on the Phase 2 util/http.py.

items.title: Re-partition Iceberg by month(fetch_ts)+source_type and add real compaction
items.why: day(fetch_ts) over a multi-year corpus + append-per-500-row-flush fragments the table into thousands of sub-MB Parquet files (pathological scan planning). Switch to month partitioning, buffer larger appends, and wire the stubbed list_pending_manifests/mark_manifest_compacted into an `awareness storage compact` command.

items.title: Export metrics (/metrics + CLI snapshot) and add per-fetch structured outcome logs + trace_id
items.why: Metrics die at CLI process exit, there's no /metrics endpoint, and fetch failures lack a consistent {url,host,status,attempt,latency,outcome} record. Add Prometheus exposition, standardized fetch_result logs/histograms, and per-task trace_id. Multiplier on every other fix's debuggability; depends on the Phase 4 histogram fix.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Data integrity & product polish
phases.goal: Close remaining data-consistency gaps and finish the product surface (UI, onboarding) so the experience matches the documentation. These depend on storage and search being correct, and are lower-urgency than getting data in and findable.

items.title: Crash-safe flush (durable-before-clear) and idempotent Iceberg appends
items.why: _flush clears the in-memory buffer before durable write (data-loss window on crash), and non-idempotent Iceberg appends silently duplicate rows that only the read-time view hides. Write durably + commit manifest before advancing state; make Iceberg a replayable derived copy fed from committed manifests.

items.title: Reconcile JSONL+Iceberg union to deterministic counts; surface iceberg_ok=False
items.why: The same rows live in JSONL and Iceberg with a fragile ROW_NUMBER reconciliation that silently changes on partial failure or post-compaction overlap; capture_id embeds observed_ts so recaptures aren't folded. Exclude compacted chunks, promote iceberg setup failure to WARNING + status flag, and add a consistency-check command.

items.title: Disentangle fetch_ts / observed_ts / published_ts semantics and pivots
items.why: fetch_ts is overloaded as both content-time and the recency/partition pivot — the deeper root cause behind the search-window bug. Define the three clearly, default recency/listings and Iceberg partitioning to observed_ts, and offer both content-time and ingest-time filters. Larger refactor; do after the immediate window bug fix (Phase 1).

items.title: Tighten URL canonicalization (trailing slash, www, index pages, case)
items.why: Under-normalization splits one logical page across multiple doc_ids/domains, inflating distinct-doc counts and fragmenting dedup groups. Normalize trailing slash, optional www-stripping, percent-encoding, with tests.

items.title: Treat unknown language as pass-through; narrow the bare-except
items.why: languages=['en'] drops every doc where detection returned None (short/mixed/error), losing genuine English. Keep on unknown, drop only on confident mismatch, make langdetect deterministic, and add a docs.dropped_by_language metric. Pairs with the Phase 4 LID upgrade.

items.title: Honor declared charset/BOM in tail recrawl (pass bytes to trafilatura)
items.why: r.text mis-decodes legacy/CJK pages that declare charset only in <meta>, storing mojibake that's unsearchable and pollutes dedup hashes. Pass r.content to trafilatura's own detection or set encoding from a meta sniff; flag high U+FFFD ratio.

items.title: Make the SPA Settings page editable (or correct the README screenshot)
items.why: The README screenshot promises editable config/source toggles/language filters; the actual Settings view is a read-only dump. Add GET/PATCH /config (backed by existing config set/unset) and editable controls — or fix the docs. Credibility/usability gap.

items.title: Defensive captures view via dynamic NULL-filling (robustness hardening)
items.why: Generalizes the Phase 1 captures-view fix into a systematic dynamic projection (introspect present columns, NULL-fill absent ones from the DocCapture schema) plus surfacing the error to callers — protects all read paths against future schema drift.

quick_wins: bug:tail-engine-jobstatus-nameerror — one-line import fix removes a deterministic crash on the documented tail resume path
bug:cli-search-default-30day-window-hides-results — change two Typer defaults to None; directly fixes the headline 'bitcoin → 2 results' symptom with no data migration
bug:jsonl-gz-corpus-invisible-to-search — change rglob('*.jsonl') to '*.jsonl*' at two lines; restores all search for compressed deployments
bug:end-date-filter-excludes-whole-day — coerce date-only end to end-of-day; stops silently dropping the most-recent full day across four endpoints
bug:gdrive-upload-readtext-fails-on-gzip-and-sends-invalid-json — read_bytes instead of read_text; fixes 100% Drive-upload failure under compression
bug:capped-indicator-never-triggers — fix the dead comparison; trivial and folds into the pagination fixes
imp:install-fineweb-deps-or-warn-loudly — either add the [hf] dep or drop FineWeb from defaults + WARN; removes a silent 1/3 ingestion loss
imp:expose-cc-wet-shard-count — plumb one config value and raise the default; orders-of-magnitude more docs per backfill
bug:relative-start-parse-silently-drops-filter / bug:search-end-parse-crash — reuse the existing BadParameter pattern; stop silent-widen and raw tracebacks on bad dates
biggest_risks: The collinfo.json crawl-ID fix (Phase 2) is the single point everything depends on, but it introduces a network dependency on index.commoncrawl.org at plan time; if the bundled fallback snapshot isn't shipped and tested, an offline/blocked user is back to zero data. The fallback list and TTL cache must be part of the same change, not a follow-up.

The atomic claim_pending_tasks fix must be DB-level, not the in-process self._lock RLock the original suggestion mentions — the per-process lock does NOT help the cross-process race (standalone awareness-worker vs API), which is the actual trigger. Getting this wrong gives false confidence while double-claims persist on Postgres/SQLite.

Several Phase 1 fixes interact and must land together or regress each other: premature-COMPLETED-on-stop + orphaned-RUNNING-reaper (a fixed COMPLETED bug still leaves RUNNING orphans unresumable), and the FTS singleton + write-write-conflict fix (the conflict fix is meaningless without the singleton). Sequencing these as independent PRs risks half-fixes.

Switching Iceberg partitioning to month(fetch_ts) (Phase 5) is a schema/partition-spec change on an existing warehouse — it is not a pure code change and needs a migration/rewrite path, or it will fragment further or fail to read old partitions.

Lowering the Hamming threshold via FPR calibration (Phase 4) and fixing banding both change which docs merge into dup_groups; combined with the union-find cluster fix, near-dup grouping semantics shift materially. Without the bootstrap-CI benchmark harness landing first, these changes can't be validated and could degrade precision in production.

The 30-day-window fix changes default search scope from 'last 30 days' to 'all time'. For a genuinely live/news use-case some users may rely on recency; without the result-header showing the active window (and a --last convenience flag), this trades one silent behavior for another surprising one.

Adding `datasets` (FineWeb) to core deps materially increases install size/footprint and pulls in pyarrow/huggingface_hub; the safer path (optional [hf] extra + remove from defaults) must be the chosen one, or fresh-install UX and CI time regress.

Wiring real HTTP retries + higher shard counts + removed fan-out caps simultaneously can turn an inert scraper into one that hammers data.commoncrawl.org/GDELT and gets rate-limited or IP-banned. The per-domain limiter fix and the job-wide budget must land alongside the breadth increases, not after.
completeness_gaps: No audit coverage of the SSRF/security posture of is_public_http_url beyond the blocking-DNS performance angle: verify the redirect-hop revalidation actually blocks private/link-local/IPv6 ULA and DNS-rebinding (resolve-then-connect TOCTOU) — adding a DNS cache (Phase 1) could itself open a rebinding window if not careful.

robots.txt compliance correctness was only touched tangentially (robots.is_allowed called on the event loop). No audit of whether crawl-delay from robots is honored, whether disallow rules are parsed correctly, or whether the User-Agent the limiter/robots uses matches the one sent on fetches — relevant before increasing shard breadth.

The Iceberg/PyIceberg write path (storage/iceberg.py append, snapshot/manifest growth, schema evolution) is largely unexamined except for partitioning; check catalog locking/concurrent-append behavior and whether append failures are surfaced or swallowed like the HTTP path.

GDELT adapter internals (gdelt.py slot enumeration, GKG parsing, the 8-slot cap, zip handling) were only referenced for the swallow-on-404 pattern; the actual correctness of slot/time math (analogous to the CC odd-week bug) was not independently verified and could be a second 'fabricated identifier' bug.

No test-suite audit: which of these bugs are covered by existing tests, and whether the proposed fixes will pass CI. Several bugs explicitly note weak/over-hedged tests (test_planner.py count-only assertion, test_dedup.py NEAR_DUP|EXACT_DUP|NEW hedge, test_search_matching.py _FULL_KEYS workaround). A coverage map is needed before refactoring.

The local_fixture and warc_repair sources got minimal scrutiny; warc_repair shares html_to_text/min_chars and the swallow pattern but its WARC parsing correctness, the WARC-Record-ID/offset handling, and its interaction with CC-Index (the cc_index→warc_repair sub-partition path) were not deeply verified.

Concurrency/locking of the state DB beyond claim_pending_tasks: increment_job_counters, complete_task, fail_task, add_tasks all run cross-process against the same SQLite file with no explicit transaction isolation — 'database is locked' errors and lost counter updates under real concurrency were not stress-tested, and SQLite WAL mode / busy_timeout configuration is unmentioned.

The /backfill/{job_id}/run endpoint spawning a fresh WorkerEngine, and the relationship between the API-spawned worker, the in-CLI worker, and the standalone awareness-worker (three ways to drain a job) was flagged for the race but the overall job-ownership/leasing model is undesigned — needs a single 'who owns this job' contract before the atomic-claim and reaper fixes.

Memory/disk growth of the JSONL staging dir over time (no rotation/compaction trigger described for the non-Iceberg path) and the DuckDB metadata.duckdb file growth across per-request connections — unbounded-growth failure modes weren't assessed.

Pydantic/schema validation of BackfillRequest and inbound API bodies (domains, languages, date strings) is minimal (jobs.py:54 has no validator); the new config knobs (shards-per-crawl, budget, fineweb-rows) need input validation and sane caps to avoid foot-guns once they're user-settable.

The dashboard/SPA (app.js) beyond search/captures — Jobs page, tail controls, dedup-stats, polling behavior, and how it handles the new 'completed_empty'/EMPTY job states and health signals — was not reviewed; UI assumptions may break when backend states/fields change.

No assessment of the `awareness init`/config-wizard flow end-to-end or whether the documented data dir/permissions/first-run paths actually exist and are writable, which matters for the quickstart (Phase 2) to reliably produce data on a fresh clone.
